title: Basic Information Staff Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) FMOS, DC I
raw_text:
7.     MOS 0510, Basic Information Staff Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) FMOS, DC I

    a. Summary. Information Practitioners are focused on the information
environment (IE), operational planning and coordination, IE characterization/
analysis, and integration of information. Duties encompass the supervision
of tasking, processing, and dissemination of products related to the thirteen
(13) different information related capabilities (IRCs), operation security
(OPSEC), military deception (MILDEC), information assurance (IA), cyberspace
operations, electronic warfare (EW), special effects, physical attack,
physical security, defense support to public diplomacy (DSPD), communications
strategy and operations (COMMSTRAT), counterintelligence (CI), civil military
operations (CMO), and military information support operations (MISO).
Advanced information planners prepare and issue reports to include target
audience analysis reports, technical reports, and summaries. This MOS will
be assigned as a non-PMOS only by the CMC (MM).

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Security requirement:     active secret security clearance.

        (2) Must be currently in or have orders to fill, an information
planner billet.


                                            1-34                        Enclosure (1)
 1108                                                                   NAVMC 1200.1L



       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the MAGTF Operations in the Information Environment
Practitioner Course (MOPC) (M02F2GD), Quantico, VA.

        (2) Any of these requirements may be waived by the Deputy Commandant
for Information based on unique work or educational experience.

       d.   Duties

            (1) Provides USMC input to DoD Information policy development.

        (2) Assists in the development of USMC doctrine on Information
consistent with USMC policy on Information.

        (3) Coordinates with representatives of other information-related
capabilities on the MAGTF staff.

        (4) Develops Information plans and Information annexes to operations
plans for all operations, contingencies and exercises.

        (5) Acts as a liaison for information-related capabilities that are
not organic to the MAGTF troop list.

        (6) Provides subject matter expertise to the development of USMC
policy on Information consistent with DoD policy.

        (7) Advises the commanding and operations officer on the conduct of
Information in order to provide continuity of Information objectives across
the range of military operations (ROMO).

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Management Analysts 13-1111.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
